messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — I'm bringing robinia-embed-v1 through onboarding. Ran the standard holdout + short-query bench and saw some odd clustering/recall behavior, want a quick sync. TL;DR: fp16 looks fine, int8 quant shows recall@1/5 drops on short queries and a few strange small clusters in UMAP.

ben: can you paste the numbers? which datasets?

anya: dataset: shorttail-collection-3 (mix of short queries from product logs + synthetic paraphrases). Baselines: albatross-v2 (prod). Quick table: 
- albatross-v2 fp16: recall@1=0.78, recall@5=0.92, silhouette=0.42
- robinia-v1 fp16: recall@1=0.81, recall@5=0.94, silhouette=0.45
- robinia-v1 int8 (per-channel symmetric): recall@1=0.66, recall@5=0.85, silhouette=0.28

carlos: that's a big drop for int8. did you do perdim rescale or only symmetric quant? any calibration set?
anya: used our usual CalSet100k (random holdout of production-like), and the quant pipeline: 
```
python quantize.py --model robinia-v1 --mode int8 --calib CalSet100k --per_channel
```
I also tried asymmetric per-tensor and saw slightly better recall@1 (~0.69) but silhouette still ~0.30.
ben: interesting that fp16 is better than baseline. Could be model architecture improvements but quantization interaction is weird. Have you plotted embedding norms / activation hist?
anya: yes. Norms shift left under int8 - mean L2 norm down ~12% vs fp16. Cosine similarity distributions for positive pairs shift from mean 0.74 (fp16) to 0.61 (int8). Negative pair dist stays about the same -> reduces margin.
eva: did you try calibrating by scaling the embeddings post-quant? like a small temp-scaling learned to match mean norm?
anya: quick experiment: apply scalar postnorm to train set (multiply embeddings by 1.14) brought recall@1 from 0.66 -> 0.71 on the holdout but overfit risk. Might be okay as a short-term mitigation.
carlos: what about clustering? small clusters you mentioned — any patterns (languages, tokens, short lengths)?
anya: UMAP colored by query length shows the weird clusters are almost exclusively <=4 tokens and high-digit tokens (IDs, codes). For natural short queries it's mixed; for code-ish short queries they collapse together. KMeans (k=200) purity for true intent labels drops from 0.61(fp16) to 0.44(int8).
ben: could be quantization amplifying token-position biases or norm clipping for short sequences. Can we check KV-cache behavior or last-layer norm?
eva: also check inference pipeline: are we using fused L2-normalize post-quant or doing float-normalize after dequant? small implementation differences can matter.
anya: good call — pipeline dequant then L2 norm in fp32. I re-ran a path where we keep dequant as float16 until after norm; that improved a point or two on recall@1. Will run a full sweep.
eval-bot: evaluation finished for robinia-v1 int8 asymmetric (run id r-2026-03-22-13): recall@1=0.70, recall@5=0.87, silhouette=0.31, notes=\"asymmetric per-tensor helped but short-query tail still low\"
carlos: please add the UMAP png to the onboarding doc and include the per-token length breakdown. Also schedule a small canary: robinia-v1 fp16 -> staged; int8 behind a fallback to albatross if recall@1 < 0.7 for short queries.
eva: for next steps I suggest: 1) per-channel vs per-tensor sweep with more calib sets (CalSet100k vs CalSet1M), 2) try 6-bit (QAT-style) and per-channel bias correction, 3) small post-quant scaling learned on validation.
anya: yep — I'll run the sweep and push results to the onboarding board. If int8 can't meet short-query thresholds we'll keep fp16 for Dedicated and reserve int8 for background batch embeddings.
ben: thanks. ping us when the sweep finishes, and put the quick reproduce commands into the thread so SRE can reproduce the canary.
anya: will do. reproducible commands in the doc now; linking after sweep. :thumbsup:
